security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU TCG helper for P-extension saturating shift instructions (PSSHL.HS, PSSHL.WS, PSSHLR.HS, PSSHLR.WS, SSHL) uses signed comparison (>_s / <_s) for unsigned saturation checks on the shifted result, causing values with the MSB set (e.g., 0x80000000) to be treated as negative and incorrectly saturate to signed min/max bounds instead of the unsigned max bound (0xFF...FF), or fail to saturate when the unsigned magnitude exceeds the unsigned max but the signed magnitude is within signed range
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: signed integer comparison against 0x7FFF... or 0x8000... in TCG helper for saturating packed shift, where the saturation target is an unsigned range; look for `>_s` or `<_s` semantics (C: `(int64_t)val > INT32_MAX` or `(int64_t)val < INT32_MIN`, or Rust-like `as i64` wrapping) where `>_u` / unsigned comparison against 0xFFFF...FFFF is required per corrected pseudocode
security_spec.summary: Spec pseudocode had copy/paste errors using signed comparisons (>_s, <_s) for unsigned saturation bounds; QEMU helpers implementing the old pseudocode would produce incorrect saturation results for values with MSB=1, corrupting guest packed SIMD computation

findings.finding: These are RISC-V V-extension (vector) saturating scaling shift helpers, not P-extension packed SIMD. vssrl* uses unsigned types (uint8_t/16/32/64) and vssra* uses signed types (int8_t/16/32/64), both matching their respective semantics. No signed/unsigned confusion bug present here.

location.function_name: PSSHL.HS / PSSHL.WS / PSSHLR.HS / PSSHLR.WS / SSHL TCG helpers

findings.finding: The RISC-V P-extension (packed SIMD/Zpn) saturating shift instructions (PSSHL.HS, PSSHL.WS, PSSHLR.HS, PSSHLR.WS, SSHL) and their TCG helpers are NOT implemented in this QEMU version. No packed SIMD helper files exist under target/riscv/ (only pmp.c and pmu.c exist; no insn_trans/trans_rvp*.c.inc). The vulnerability pattern (signed vs unsigned saturation comparison) is not applicable because the code simply does not exist in this codebase.
This is the only modified file in the current working tree (6-line addition adding a validation check for MSI translation when IOMMU mode is BARE). Unrelated to P-extension shift instructions.
